title: A Desire to Be Understood
content_text:
A Desire to Be Understood
[2025年10月13日——渴望被理解]
During today’s project progress meeting, I found myself constantly explaining why an issue had taken so long to resolve — essentially hoping others would understand my situation.
[在今天的项目进度会议上，我一直在解释为什么一个问题花了这么长时间还没有解决——其实内心是在希望别人能理解我。]
But upon reflection, I realized the real focus should have been on identifying the core problem, figuring out how to solve it, determining whether I needed help, and clarifying the target timeline.
[但事后冷静下来，我意识到真正的重点应该是：问题出在哪里、该如何解决、是否需要他人帮助，以及目标完成时间是什么。]
Why did I instinctively crave others’ understanding? Was it a lack of confidence deep down? An attempt to shift responsibility? Or perhaps a subtle desire for sympathy?
[为什么我下意识地渴望别人理解？是因为内心缺乏自信？想推卸责任？还是想博取他人的同情？]
By the end of the day, I felt a sense of confusion — a realization that I need to approach problems in a structured, methodical, and organized way. I shouldn’t settle for vague explanations or try to gloss things over.
[一天结束时，我感到有些混乱——这让我意识到，自己需要以更有条理、更系统、更有方法的方式去分析和解决问题，而不是停留在模糊的解释或敷衍的应对上。]
In light of what I’ve learned about the “creative structure,” I should aim to create a proactive version of myself — one who seeks information, drives progress, and takes initiative — rather than passively reacting to problems or waiting for direction.
[结合之前学到的“创造型结构”，我应该去创造一个主动获取信息、推动项目进展、积极行动的自己，而不是被动地应对问题或等待他人的指挥。]
